list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: Panels reference ${datasource} instead of a uid baked into the JSON: the uid is provisioned from git (datasource.yml -> 'prometheus'), and a uid handmade in the UI is how a promoted dashboard ends up pointed at a datasource that does not exist.

list.name: job
list.label: Scrape job
list.description: Which scrape path produced a series: 'llm-server' is the direct target, 'llm-server-via-proxy' is monitor/serve.py's passthrough (by default it carries only llm_monitor_* — see monitoring/README.md, 'The two llm scrape jobs'). 'prometheus' is the self-scrape and has no model series, so leaving it selected is harmless. Derived from up, so the list is empty rather than wrong when nothing is being scraped.

list.name: instance
list.label: Instance
list.description: host:port of a scrape target, from up/instance. monitor/serve.py's Grafana deep links set var-instance to the upstream's host:port, which is the mapping that makes a link from the live page land on the right series. Declared after $job so it narrows with it.

list.name: model
list.label: Model
list.description: Only servers that are labelled show up: llama.cpp does not label its own metrics at all (the `model` here normally comes from monitoring/prometheus/targets/llm-servers.json file_sd labels), and vLLM's own label is model_name, which the llm:* recording rules normalize onto `model` — hence the alias in the selector. An empty list means no model label anywhere: All (.*) then keeps every panel working, and the per-model panel draws one line called 'unknown'.

panels.title: requests in flight
panels.description:
Instant gauges, no rate(): `sum(llamacpp:requests_processing)` and `sum(llamacpp:requests_deferred)` (halogen's `requests_running` / `requests_queued` spellings match too).

deferred > 0 means arrivals are waiting for a slot — the earliest sign the KV budget is the limit.

'No data' here means one of: this server publishes no /metrics at all (the monitor page still works — it reads /health, /v1/models and /cache, which are not Prometheus metrics), the scrape target is down, or this build does not expose this family. The Scrape health row says which.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum({__name__=~"llamacpp:requests_processing|halogen:requests_running|vllm:num_requests_running",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"})
A: sum({__name__=~"llamacpp:requests_deferred|halogen:requests_queued|vllm:num_requests_waiting",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"})
```

panels.title: KV cache used
panels.description:
`max(llamacpp:kv_cache_usage_ratio)` — the same series the LLMKVCachePressure alerts read, so this tile and a page cannot disagree. 1 = 100 % of the pool.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: max({__name__=~"llamacpp:kv_cache_usage_ratio|llamacpp:kv_cache_usage",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"})
```

panels.title: decode tok/s
panels.description:
Instant read of the same rate() as the decode panel below: windowed throughput right now, not a lifetime average.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total|vllm:generation_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
```

panels.title: prompt-cache hit ratio
panels.description:
The windowed ratio from the Cache & KV row as a single number. llama.cpp's prompt_tokens_total counts cache MISSES, hence the `+ cached` in the denominator.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"halogen:prompt_tokens_cached_total|llamacpp:prompt_cache_tokens_cached_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:prompt_tokens_total|vllm:prompt_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum(rate({__name__=~"halogen:prompt_tokens_cached_total|llamacpp:prompt_cache_tokens_cached_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), 1)
```

panels.title: draft acceptance
panels.description:
Instant value of the speculative-decode acceptance ratio plotted in the Speculative decode row. No data simply means this server is not speculating (no draft counters) — not that speculation is failing.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"halogen:draft_tokens_accepted_total|llamacpp:draft_tokens_accepted_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate({__name__=~"halogen:draft_tokens_total|llamacpp:draft_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), 1)
```

defaults.noValue: no speculative decode on this server

panels.title: TTFT p99
panels.description:
Instant value of panel 3's p99. 'No histogram' means exactly that: this build exposes no time_to_first_token histogram, so the server's own log is the only latency source (see the Latency row).

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:ttft_seconds_bucket|vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
```

defaults.noValue: no histogram on this server

panels.title: Decode throughput (tok/s)
panels.description:
Windowed rate over the generation-token counter, summed across whatever survives the $job / $instance / $model filters, plus three reference lines:

* **{{instance}}** — the same rate per target, so two servers on one box stay separate lines instead of being silently added together;
* **server gauge** — `llamacpp:predicted_tokens_seconds`, the server's own 'average since last scrape' number, which is what the bespoke page rendered. Overlaid deliberately during the migration so the two definitions are comparable, and the first thing workspace-szw.11 deletes once rate() is trusted. Where they disagree, rate() is right: the gauge resets with the process and knows nothing about the window;
* **(rule)** — the `llm:decode_tokens_per_second` alias.

This is the panel that answers 'what was decode throughput at 03:00', which the bespoke page could not answer at all.

rate() needs two points, so the line starts at least one scrape interval in. A counter reset (server restart) shows as a gap, not a spike to zero.

Series tagged `(rule)` are the neutral llm:* aliases from monitoring/prometheus/recording_rules.yml — the vendor-drift seam ADR 0001 C3 names, and what alert rules should read. They are plotted *alongside* the raw expression, not instead of it, on purpose: a panel must still render against a server whose rules have never run, and 'No data' has to mean no data rather than no rule. Where the two disagree the rule is stale — or the windows differ: rules use a fixed 5m, panels use $__rate_interval.

$job / $instance / $model default to All, whose allValue is .*, so an absent label widens the selector instead of emptying the panel.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total|vllm:generation_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
A: sum by (instance, job) (rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total|vllm:generation_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
A: sum({__name__=~"llamacpp:predicted_tokens_seconds|llamacpp:tokens_predicted_seconds",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"})
A: llm:decode_tokens_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
```

panels.title: Prompt throughput (tok/s)
panels.description:
Prefill throughput: windowed rate over the prompt-token counter.

llama.cpp counts only the prompt tokens that MISSED the prompt cache in this counter (halogen counts the served-from-cache ones separately), which is why the cache panel computes cached / (processed + cached) instead of cached / processed. `llamacpp:prompt_tokens_seconds` (the server's own average gauge) is overlaid for the same migration reason as on the decode panel, and leaves with it.

rate() needs two points, so the line starts at least one scrape interval in. A counter reset (server restart) shows as a gap, not a spike to zero.

Series tagged `(rule)` are the neutral llm:* aliases from monitoring/prometheus/recording_rules.yml — the vendor-drift seam ADR 0001 C3 names, and what alert rules should read. They are plotted *alongside* the raw expression, not instead of it, on purpose: a panel must still render against a server whose rules have never run, and 'No data' has to mean no data rather than no rule. Where the two disagree the rule is stale — or the windows differ: rules use a fixed 5m, panels use $__rate_interval.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:prompt_tokens_total|vllm:prompt_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
A: sum by (instance, job) (rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:prompt_tokens_total|vllm:prompt_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
A: sum({__name__=~"llamacpp:prompt_tokens_seconds",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"})
A: llm:prompt_tokens_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
```

panels.title: Requests running / queued
panels.description:
Gauges, not rates: running vs deferred vs configured slot capacity. `deferred > 0` for minutes is queueing, and LLMQueueing in rules.yml fires on this same expression, so the panel and the alert cannot disagree.

Deferred > 0 while running < slot capacity is a scheduling stall; deferred > 0 at full slots is plain saturation. Different incidents, and this is the panel that tells them apart.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum({__name__=~"llamacpp:requests_processing|halogen:requests_running|vllm:num_requests_running",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"})
A: sum({__name__=~"llamacpp:requests_deferred|halogen:requests_queued|vllm:num_requests_waiting",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"})
A: sum({__name__=~"halogen:slot_capacity",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"})
A: llm:requests_running{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
A: llm:requests_queued{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
```

panels.title: Requests / s and structured share
panels.description:
Request rate from the completed-request counter, and the fraction of requests decoded under a JSON schema (`halogen:structured_requests_total / halogen:requests_total`).

The structured share is the useful one when a client changes behaviour: a schema jump usually precedes a decode-rate change, because grammar-constrained decoding does not overlap speculation well.

rate() needs two points, so the line starts at least one scrape interval in. A counter reset (server restart) shows as a gap, not a spike to zero.

clamp_min(<denominator>, 1) is deliberate. With no traffic the raw division is 0/0, PromQL turns that into NaN and Grafana drops the sample — a hole in the line that reads like a missing metric. A clamped 0 reads as 'no ratio to report', which is the truth. The bespoke page hid the same case behind divide() (monitor/static/app.js), which is one reason this panel exists.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"halogen:requests_total|llamacpp:requests_total|vllm:request_success_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
A: sum by (instance, job) (rate({__name__=~"halogen:requests_total|llamacpp:requests_total|vllm:request_success_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"halogen:structured_requests_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate({__name__=~"halogen:requests_total|llamacpp:requests_total|vllm:request_success_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), 1)
A: llm:requests_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
```

panels.title: Decode tok/s per model
panels.description:
The per-model comparison the bespoke page could not do. `label_replace` folds llama.cpp's file_sd `model` label and vLLM's `model_name` onto one `model` label and turns 'no model label at all' into the literal `unknown`, so the legend is never blank. The $model filter is applied to both spellings (`{model=~'$model'} or {model_name=~'$model'}`) because PromQL cannot match 'either of two labels' in one selector and `label_match()` is an optional 3.x extension this box does not assume. The `(rule)` line is the same answer computed by Prometheus, where the rules normalize the label once.

On one llama.cpp server with no model label you get exactly one line called 'unknown' — correct, not broken. Name the model in the labels of monitoring/prometheus/targets/llm-servers.json to get a name here.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum by (model) (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (job, instance, model, model_name) (rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total|vllm:generation_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (job, instance, model, model_name) (rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total|vllm:generation_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model_name=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), "model", "$1", "model_name", "(.+)"), "model", "unknown", "model", "^$"))
A: sum by (model) (label_replace(label_replace(llm:decode_tokens_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}, "model", "$1", "model_name", "(.+)"), "model", "unknown", "model", "^$"))
```

targets.expr: sum by (model) (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (job, instance, model, model_name) (rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total|vllm:generation_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (job, instance, model, model_name) (rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total|vllm:generation_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model_name=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), "model", "$1", "model_name", "(.+)"), "model", "unknown", "model", "^$"))

panels.title: Decode tok/s — one panel per $instance
panels.description:
Repeat-by-variable: Grafana clones this panel for each selected $instance value, so N servers get N charts instead of N lines competing for one axis. The expression is the per-target rate, so a clone carries its own instance only.

Pin $instance to specific targets for a guaranteed one-panel-per-server; with All selected the clone set is whatever Grafana expands All to.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum by (instance, job) (rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total|vllm:generation_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
```

panels.title: Lifetime tok/s — the arithmetic the old tile did
panels.description:
Two raw counters divided, no window: what `monitor/static/app.js` rendered before Prometheus existed here. Kept on purpose, as a floor to sanity-check the windowed rates against and as the thing to delete with the JS once parity is signed off (workspace-szw.11).

It cannot say WHEN anything was slow, it averages the whole lifetime since start, and a restart silently re-bases it — which is the entire argument for the panels above.

clamp_min(<denominator>, 1) is deliberate. With no traffic the raw division is 0/0, PromQL turns that into NaN and Grafana drops the sample — a hole in the line that reads like a missing metric. A clamped 0 reads as 'no ratio to report', which is the truth. The bespoke page hid the same case behind divide() (monitor/static/app.js), which is one reason this panel exists.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: sum({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total|vllm:generation_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}) / clamp_min(sum({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_seconds_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_seconds_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}), 1)
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total|vllm:generation_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
```

panels.title: Before you read 'no histogram' on this row
panels.description:
Quantiles need `_bucket` series. A `llama-server` that exposes counters and average gauges only — which is what most builds actually do — cannot answer p99 TTFT, and no dashboard can. Those panels therefore say **no histogram on this server** instead of the useless "No data", and each one also plots the arithmetic mean from `_sum` / `_count`, which exists even when buckets do not.

The census panel at the bottom of this row states which latency families each instance publishes, so 'is this empty because of me or because of the server?' is answerable here rather than with curl.

panels.title: Time to first token — p50 / p90 / p99
panels.description:
Prefill + queue time before the first token: the latency a user actually notices, and the one the bespoke page could not render at all.

`sum by (le)` happens *before* histogram_quantile: averaging per-series quantiles is meaningless, and aggregating first is what lets several servers or models share one honest line instead of shifting each other's answer. `le` must survive that aggregation because it is what histogram_quantile reads.

The `(rule)` series are the recorded `llm:time_to_first_token_seconds:*` quantiles (ADR 0001 C3, added with these panels); if a rule is missing or stale the raw series still draw.

Series tagged `(rule)` are the neutral llm:* aliases from monitoring/prometheus/recording_rules.yml — the vendor-drift seam ADR 0001 C3 names, and what alert rules should read. They are plotted *alongside* the raw expression, not instead of it, on purpose: a panel must still render against a server whose rules have never run, and 'No data' has to mean no data rather than no rule. Where the two disagree the rule is stale — or the windows differ: rules use a fixed 5m, panels use $__rate_interval.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:ttft_seconds_bucket|vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
A: histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:ttft_seconds_bucket|vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
A: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:ttft_seconds_bucket|vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"llama:time_to_first_token_seconds_sum|llamacpp:time_to_first_token_seconds_sum|llamacpp:ttft_seconds_sum|vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_sum",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate({__name__=~"llama:time_to_first_token_seconds_count|llamacpp:time_to_first_token_seconds_count|llamacpp:ttft_seconds_count|vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_count",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), 1)
A: llm:time_to_first_token_seconds:p50{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
A: llm:time_to_first_token_seconds:p90{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
A: llm:time_to_first_token_seconds:p99{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
```

defaults.noValue: no histogram on this server (averages only, if even those exist)

panels.title: Time per output token — p50 / p90 / p99
panels.description:
Decode latency per generated token: how fast text streams once it has started. Roughly the reciprocal of tokens/s for one request, but the distribution is the point — a p99 here is a stall in the middle of a completion, which any throughput average hides.

Families differ by build (`time_per_output_token_seconds` vs `time_per_token_seconds`), which is what the name union is for.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_per_token_seconds_bucket|vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
A: histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_per_token_seconds_bucket|vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
A: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_per_token_seconds_bucket|vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"llama:time_per_output_token_seconds_sum|llamacpp:time_per_output_token_seconds_sum|llamacpp:time_per_token_seconds_sum|vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_sum",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate({__name__=~"llama:time_per_output_token_seconds_count|llamacpp:time_per_output_token_seconds_count|llamacpp:time_per_token_seconds_count|vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_count",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), 1)
A: llm:time_per_output_token_seconds:p99{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
```

defaults.noValue: no histogram on this server (averages only, if even those exist)

panels.title: End-to-end request time — p50 / p90 / p99
panels.description:
Queue + prefill + decode for a whole request. It moves *before* the throughput panels when the box is oversubscribed, which is why it sits next to TTFT rather than in a row of its own.

End-to-end growing while TTFT is flat means generation is being starved (KV pressure, speculation failing); both growing together means prefill or queueing.

'No data' here means one of: this server publishes no /metrics at all (the monitor page still works — it reads /health, /v1/models and /cache, which are not Prometheus metrics), the scrape target is down, or this build does not expose this family. The Scrape health row says which.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:end_to_end_response_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:end_to_end_response_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:requests_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:request_seconds_bucket|vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
A: histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:end_to_end_response_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:end_to_end_response_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:requests_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:request_seconds_bucket|vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
A: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:end_to_end_response_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:end_to_end_response_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:requests_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:request_seconds_bucket|vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_bucket",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
A: sum(rate({__name__=~"llama:end_to_end_response_seconds_sum|llamacpp:end_to_end_response_seconds_sum|llamacpp:requests_seconds_sum|llamacpp:request_seconds_sum|vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_sum",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate({__name__=~"llama:end_to_end_response_seconds_count|llamacpp:end_to_end_response_seconds_count|llamacpp:requests_seconds_count|llamacpp:request_seconds_count|vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds_count",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), 1)
A: llm:end_to_end_response_seconds:p99{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
```

panels.title: KV-cache pressure over time
panels.description:
The 'was the KV cache full overnight?' panel: widen the range to 12h or 24h and the answer is on the chart. Same series the LLMKVCachePressure alerts read, so this panel and a page cannot disagree.

Bands are drawn at 80 % and 90 % as visual guides; the alert numbers that actually ship live in `prometheus/alert_thresholds.env` (warn 0.90, critical 0.97) — the bands deliberately sit *below* the alerts so the chart warns before the pager does. `1h average` separates a spike from a sustained squeeze, and the per-instance lines keep two servers apart.

panels.title: Prompt-cache hit ratio + draft-accept ratio
panels.description:
The two ratios the bespoke page divided by hand in JavaScript, now as windowed rates:

* cache hit ratio = `rate(prompt_tokens_cached_total) / (rate(prompt_tokens_total) + rate(prompt_tokens_cached_total))` — the `+ cached` in the denominator is the llama.cpp convention (prompt_tokens_total counts misses only);
* draft acceptance = `rate(draft_tokens_accepted_total) / rate(draft_tokens_total)`.

Plotted together because they explain each other: a cold prompt cache and a collapsing draft-accept ratio together mean something restarted, or slots are evicting each other's prefixes — which is what LLMPromptCacheCold pages on.

clamp_min(<denominator>, 1) is deliberate. With no traffic the raw division is 0/0, PromQL turns that into NaN and Grafana drops the sample — a hole in the line that reads like a missing metric. A clamped 0 reads as 'no ratio to report', which is the truth. The bespoke page hid the same case behind divide() (monitor/static/app.js), which is one reason this panel exists.

Series tagged `(rule)` are the neutral llm:* aliases from monitoring/prometheus/recording_rules.yml — the vendor-drift seam ADR 0001 C3 names, and what alert rules should read. They are plotted *alongside* the raw expression, not instead of it, on purpose: a panel must still render against a server whose rules have never run, and 'No data' has to mean no data rather than no rule. Where the two disagree the rule is stale — or the windows differ: rules use a fixed 5m, panels use $__rate_interval.

```promql

A: sum(rate({__name__=~"halogen:draft_tokens_accepted_total|llamacpp:draft_tokens_accepted_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate({__name__=~"halogen:draft_tokens_total|llamacpp:draft_tokens_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), 1)
A: llm:prompt_cache_hit_ratio{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
A: llm:draft_acceptance_ratio{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",model=~"$model"}
```

panels.title: Prompt cache: served from cache vs reprocessed
panels.description:
The two halves of the ratio above in tokens/s, because a ratio alone cannot tell a good day from an idle one: 100 % hit on two requests is not 100 % hit on two thousand.

`served from cache` climbing while `reprocessed` stays flat is the cache doing its job. Both falling together means the prefix changed — a rebuilt system prompt, a model swap, a restart — and every TTFT after it pays for that work.

rate() needs two points, so the line starts at least one scrape interval in. A counter reset (server restart) shows as a gap, not a spike to zero.

panels.title: Read this before the charts: GPU memory on this box
panels.description:
This box is a shared-memory APU (gfx1151), so there is no separate pool of graphics memory in any useful sense:

* **GTT is the pool the model grows.** Weights, KV cache and activations are GTT (TTM) allocations; `node_drm_memory_gtt_size_bytes` is the `amdgpu.gttsize=120000` from the root README, and the used/size ratio is the pressure the stack was blind to before this row existed.
* **VRAM is the BIOS carve-out**, deliberately minimised in the BIOS (*Dedicated Graphics Memory*). It barely moves and it is **never** an alert — it is plotted so a mistake in the BIOS or the driver shows up as a flat line, not as a mystery.
* **GTT is system RAM**, so GPU exhaustion and host exhaustion are the same event: the *Host companion* panel (memory PSI, swap, load) is not a bonus, it is the other half of the question.
* Nothing here needs ROCm: these are amdgpu **kernel driver** attributes, and the Vulkan path llama.cpp uses reads the same sysfs the ROCm path would. No `/dev/kfd`, no root, and the exporter is bound to loopback only.

Absent is not zero. node_exporter publishes an attribute it could not read as `0` rather than omitting it (the findings note §1.1 explains why: the driver refuses to answer rather than waking a runtime-suspended card), so `0 %` busy or a `0` sensor can mean *could not ask*. A high number is always real; a low one may not be. `python3 spikes/amd-gpu-metrics/amdgpu_sysfs_probe.py probe` prints the same attributes with the honest ok/missing/denied/busy status.

Every `node_*` series on this row comes from the `host` scrape job (node_exporter on the host, `prometheus/targets/host.json`). If this panel is empty while the model panels are fine, the exporter or the scrape path is the problem, not the GPU: `NodeExporterAbsent` / `NodeGpuTelemetryAbsent` say which, and monitoring/README.md has the decision tree. Pinning `$job` to a model job also empties this row on purpose — a host has no model job.

panels.title: GTT headroom
panels.description:
`min(GTT size - GTT used)` — the bytes left before an allocation fails, which is the number that decides whether the next request or the next model fits. Absolute, because 'how much is enough' depends on what you are about to load, not on a percentage.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: min({__name__=~"node_drm_memory_gtt_size_bytes",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"} - {__name__=~"node_drm_memory_gtt_used_bytes",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"})
```

defaults.noValue: no GPU telemetry (host job down?)

panels.title: GPU busy
panels.description:
`max(node_drm_gpu_busy_percent)` — the driver's own load figure (SMU average gfx activity on this part). Read it against decode tok/s on the Overview row: busy high and tok/s low is a thermally or memory-throttled box, busy low and tok/s low is an idle one.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: max({__name__=~"node_drm_gpu_busy_percent",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"})
```

defaults.noValue: no gpu_busy_percent (see panel note: absent is not 0)

panels.title: hottest GPU sensor
panels.description:
`max(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{chip="amdgpu"})` — the hottest of the GPU's sensors, whichever the kernel names them (gfx1151's sensor names are only knowable on the box; `node_hwmon_chip_names` is the lookup). On this class of part the junction maximum is about 100 °C, which is why the bands match the two alerts.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: max(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{chip="amdgpu",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"})
```

defaults.noValue: no amdgpu hwmon temp exposed

panels.title: memory PSI
panels.description:
`max(rate(node_pressure_memory_waiting_seconds_total[...]))` — the share of wall clock with at least one task stalled on memory. This is the same expression NodeMemoryPressure{High,Critical} alert on, and on a box whose GPU memory *is* system RAM it is the earliest warning either half produces.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: max(rate({__name__=~"node_pressure_memory_waiting_seconds_total",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))
```

defaults.noValue: no PSI on this kernel

panels.title: drm collector
panels.description:
`node_scrape_collector_success{collector="drm"}` — 1 means the GPU half of this row was actually collected on the last scrape. It is on this row and not only on Scrape health because the failure mode here is silent: a containerised exporter with a partial `/sys` mount, or a kernel that stopped binding the card, takes the whole row down without taking node_exporter down.

PromQL sent by this panel:

```promql
A: {__name__=~"node_scrape_collector_success",collector="drm",job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}
```

defaults.noValue: no host scrape at all
